lines.trans: Fyodor, prepare two portions of shrimp.
A chef should shout at cooks!
Arseny, you deserve respectful treatment.
But strict discipline is needed in the kitchen.
You have the cleanest workstation.
Where is the hot dish for table three?
The guests have been waiting forty minutes already!
Sasha, calmly, let us breathe deeply.
This dish takes over an hour to cook.
They threaten to leave without paying.
Ask the guests to wait a little longer.
New order: partridge and mushrooms.
We will make everything on time, chef!
Arseny, you deserve respectful treatment.
You have the cleanest workstation.
Sasha, calmly, let us breathe deeply.
Ask the guests to wait a little longer.
Fyodor, prepare two portions of shrimp.
A chef should shout at cooks!
Arseny, you deserve respectful treatment.
But strict discipline is needed in the kitchen.
You have the cleanest workstation.
Where is the hot dish for table three?
The guests have been waiting forty minutes already!
Sasha, calmly, let us breathe deeply.
This dish takes over an hour to cook.
They threaten to leave without paying.
Ask the guests to wait a little longer.
New order: partridge and mushrooms.
We will make everything on time, chef!
Politeness always yields an excellent result.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'without' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: That's no problem.
This time there's no trick.
That's no problem at all.

meanings.note: a particular prepared food item or meal course

examples.trans: This is a dish, course.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more'.
Secondary conversational sense ('bigger') (comparative of большой) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.
I don't need any more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'politeness, courtesy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Politeness always yields an excellent result.

examples.text: В хорошем ресторане вежливость важна для каждого официанта.
examples.trans: In a good restaurant, courtesy is important for every waiter.

вовремя.gloss: on time, at the right moment

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'on time'.

examples.trans: Bad timing!
He always comes on time.

examples.text: Ну как же ты не вовремя! Где ты сейчас?
examples.trans: Your timing couldn't be worse! Where are you now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's always like that.
There's always a way out.
She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'where'.

examples.trans: Where's my toy car?
Where's Dad?

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'deeply'.

examples.trans: I genuinely like you deeply.
He took a deep breath.

examples.text: Ты мне даже глубоко симпатичен, Аркаша.
examples.trans: I even genuinely like you, Arkasha.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea.
Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.
You have visitors!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'приготовиться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: We are simply preparing for the morning show.
The students were preparing for the exam.
And little Grisha is preparing for the morning show.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'mushroom' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I love mushrooms.
This is a bad mushroom.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to threaten', paired with 'пригрозить'.

examples.trans: They threaten to leave without paying.

examples.text: Они грозятся уйти из ресторана без оплаты.
examples.trans: They are threatening to leave the restaurant without paying.

examples.text: Шеф опять грозится уволить всю кухню за опоздание.
examples.trans: The chef is again threatening to fire the whole kitchen for being late.

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.trans: Let's talk.
He gives me a book.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.trans: In two weeks.
Two houses.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'discipline' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Strict discipline is needed in the kitchen.

examples.text: Но на кухне нужна строгая дисциплина.
examples.trans: But strict discipline is needed in the kitchen.
Do not teach me discipline!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Secondary conversational sense ('owe') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have to work.
Greed should be moderate.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: достойная старость = a comfortable, dignified old age

examples.text: А мы обеспечим вам достойную старость.
examples.trans: And we will ensure you a comfortable old age.
That is a worthy answer.

examples.text: Отдайте это видео мне. А мы обеспечим вам достойную старость.
examples.trans: Give this video to me. And we will ensure you a comfortable old age.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to breathe'.

examples.trans: Breathe, son!
I can't breathe.

examples.text: Лёша, что случилось? Дыши, сынок, дыши!
examples.trans: Lyosha, what happened? Breathe, son, breathe!

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('even (with comparatives)') (ещё больше = even more) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'подождать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to expect') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Don't wait for me.
I'm waiting for you.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'order', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('booking') (commission or reservation) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я делаю всё точно по вашему заказу.
examples.trans: I do everything exactly according to your order.
In the kitchen they are preparing this order.
The waiter took the order.

meanings.en: to deserve, merit, be worthy of
meanings.note: imperfective, governs accusative or genitive

examples.trans: He deserves respect.

examples.text: Макс вполне заслуживает хороший урок, знаешь.
examples.trans: Max quite deserves a good lesson, you know.
Arseny, you deserve respectful treatment.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'shrimp, prawn' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Prepare two portions of shrimp.
Fyodor, prepare two portions of shrimp.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to shout', forming an aspectual pair with 'крикнуть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: There's no need to shout.
Why are you shouting?

examples.text: Не надо кричать. Хорошо, я буду сегодня.
examples.trans: There's no need to shout. All right, I'll be there tonight.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'partridge'.

examples.trans: The cook skillfully prepared tender partridge.

examples.text: Куропатка оставалась, а выбрасывать было жалко.
examples.trans: Partridge was left over, and it was a shame to throw it out.

examples.text: Нет, Федя сам жарил эту куропатку!
examples.trans: No, Fedya roasted that partridge himself!

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We're sitting in the kitchen.
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: in 'рабочее место' = workplace, job
Secondary conversational sense ('post, position') (на его место = in his place) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: This is my seat.
It's a nice place here.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.
Just a minute!

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.trans: A new house.
I need a new job.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job

examples.trans: I need a job too.
Do you need a pen?
He needs money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ращение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'treatment, address' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You deserve respectful treatment.
Arseny, you deserve respectful treatment.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('they') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.trans: They are building a centre.
History will punish them.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'payment' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They will leave without paying.
They threaten to leave without paying.
This cognac goes to payment.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat.
An excellent area!

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: There is this English chef.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask (for), to request', paired with 'просить'.

examples.trans: I wanted to ask you something.
Ask Mum.
Arkash, I wanted to ask you something.

meanings.note: International borrowing in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), declined as a regular feminine noun meaning 'portion'.

examples.trans: The waiter brought two portions of salad.

examples.text: И ещё две порции трески с миндалём!
examples.trans: And two more portions of cod with almonds!
Fyodor, prepare two portions of shrimp.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'готовить'.

examples.trans: I made a cake.
Mum cooked a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'working', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('worker') (as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: That means thousands of jobs.
A working day.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'result' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас.
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you.
This is an excellent result of the work.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас. Работайте!
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you. Get to work!

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: сорок рублей; other cases: сорока

examples.trans: I'm forty.
There are forty million here.
I don't know. Forty, I think.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You'll do everything calmly.
He sat calmly.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'small table'.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трогий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strict, stern').

examples.trans: How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

examples.text: У нас в школе очень строгий директор.
examples.trans: We have a very strict principal at our school.

examples.text: Ой, спина не разгибается! Какая вы строгая, Клавдия Викторовна.
examples.trans: Ow, my back won't straighten! How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

meanings.note: ordinal numeral: в третьем поколении = third-generation

examples.trans: This is my third time.
He lives on the third floor.

examples.text: Ты что, мафия? Ты же завхоз в третьем поколении.
examples.trans: What are you, the mafia? You're a supply manager, third generation.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (on foot)', paired with 'уходить'.

examples.trans: I want him to leave.
She has already gone home.
So should I leave?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hour', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('o'clock') (в два часа = at two o'clock) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'll be there in an hour.
It's three o'clock now.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

час.governs: after 2, 3, 4 and полтора the genitive часа is stressed on the ending

meanings.note: short form чисто: всё чисто = everything is clean
Secondary conversational sense ('pure') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything is clean.
A clean floor.

examples.text: Нин, я всё помыл. Всё чисто.
examples.trans: Nina, I washed everything. It's all clean.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!
